defect_interactions.interaction_type: microband boundaries formed by geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs)
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The different contrast between microbands and matrix reflects a misorientation between either side; the boundaries are geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) formed to accommodate the misorientation between adjacent boundaries.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: dislocation pile-ups at intersections of non-coplanar slip bands
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Dislocations in the slip bands were approximately parallel and dislocation pile-ups were found at the intersections of the slip bands; the interaction was not strong enough to completely impede dislocation glide.

interfaces.phase_evolution: With increasing cold rolling reduction the deformation substructure evolves approximately in the sequence: Taylor lattice → microbands → twins → shear bands → dislocation tangles. At 50% reduction microbands and nano-twins coexist with the refined Taylor lattice.

phase_interfaces.coherence: twin–matrix (T-M) lamellar interface (coherent twin boundary; parallel {111} twin plane)

interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar dislocation glide dominates; slip bands approximately parallel with weak interaction at intersections. Cross slip is activated only at higher rolling degrees (90%).

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: High Mn–Al–C austenitic low-density steel with the nominal component Fe–30Mn–11Al–1.2C (wt%) was fabricated by vacuum induction melting method.
To homogenize and refine microstructure the cast was soaked at 1250 °C for 12 h.
Hot-forged into bars 60 mm in diameter with the finish forging temperature of 900 °C.
Sheets of various thicknesses were solution treated at 1100 °C for 1 h before cold rolling.
Cold rolled to 50% thickness reduction after solution treatment at 1100 °C for 1 h; boundary condition between stage I (10%–50%) and stage II (70%–90%) reduction regimes.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Uniaxial tensile test using SHIMADZU AG-X 50KN universal testing machine; three parallel tests per condition
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: dog-bone-shaped specimen cut along the rolling direction; gauge length 16 mm, width 4 mm

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering (Fig. 1(a)) and true (Fig. 1(b)) stress–strain curves for the 50% reduction condition are plotted; no numeric values are labelled on the curve.

defects.type: slip bands / Taylor lattice; average slip band spacing 64 nm

grain_structure.texture: Weak rolling texture; {112}<111> Cu and {123}<111> S components increase up to 50% reduction then decrease; the copper-type to brass-type texture transition occurs at 50% rolling reduction; a weak CuT ({552}<115>) component appears after 50%.

phases_present.morphology: multiple slip bands / Taylor lattice (low-energy dislocation structure)

defects.type: microbands; average width 166 nm; boundaries are geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs)
nano-scale deformation twins; average thickness ~5.1 nm; high dislocation density in twin

phases_present.morphology: very fine parallel lamellae (intermittent linear structures)

structures.overall_structure: After 50% cold rolling the single slip bands are hardly distinguishable; it is still a low-energy dislocation structure of Taylor-lattice type with refined slip band spacing (average 64 nm), while microbands (average width 166 nm) and nano-sized deformation twins (average thickness ~5.1 nm) form in some grains. Banded features lie oblique to the rolling direction (Fig. 3(c)).
